PUBLIC NOTICE

Girdwood Trails Committee is applying for Recreational Trails Program Grant Funds.
Project Title:              Girdwood Beaver Pond Trail
Description:   Restoration of the existing trail, including brushing, trail maintenance, addition of culverts and
gravel and restoration of water crossings to bring the trail to Class 3 Hiking parameters.

https://dot.alaska.gov/atlas/multi-use-trails/

Date Noticed               9/21/26

RTP grant funding for maintenance of the Girdwood Beaver Pond Trail to bring the trail up to the Trail Management
objectives (TMO) called for in the Girdwood Trails Management Plan. Several sections have poor drainage, failing
boardwalks and overgrown vegetation that needs to be brushed back. Bridge replacements are needed for some
creek crossings.

The existing trail alignment will not change, but it will be improved to the specifications called out in the TMO.

With the RTP grant, we’re seeking funding to hire a professional trail crew to complete several hitches on the trail
for repairs/improvements and to cover the materials (lumber, ground fabric, gravel, equipment) needed for those
improvements. Before starting work, we will conduct a conditions survey of the trail to identify priority areas for
repair and improvement that fit the funding we have available.

September 27, 2026    Public Notice from Girdwood Nordic Ski Club
WEST Bridge Replacement on Nordic 5K Loop
The letter serves as Public Notice of the Girdwood Nordic Ski Club’s (GNSC) proposal to
replace three log stringer bridges on the Nordic 5K Loop (installed in 2009, 2010) with culverts.
These bridge sites are all unnamed tributaries of Moose Meadow Creek, and the latter is listed in
the Anadromous Waters Catalog (AWC).
The GNSC has contracted with HDR (The Boutet Company subcontracted) to survey, design,
prepare environmental permit applications for the two culvert replacements and one fish passage,
and pursue a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Nationwide permit for maintenance
activities. Alaska Department of Fish and Game Fish Habitat permits will be issued out of the
Anchorage Habitat office, and an Alaska Department of Natural Resources Temporary Water
Use Permits.
The Girdwood Nordic Ski Club will begin replacing the bridges in Summer 2027 as funding
permits. We will start with the west bridge.
If you have any public comment or opposition about this project, please contact:
Deb Essex by December 31, 2026
Contact: deb@skigirdwood.org or PO Box 337, Girdwood AK 99587, 900-375-1720.





      Girdwood 5K Loop


The Alaska Recreational Trails Program is the possible funding agency for this proposed project.
For information regarding the Alaska Recreational Trails Program, please visit the State website
at http://dnr.alaska.gov/parks/grants/trails.htm.

I am seeking a letter of support from the Girdwood Trails Committee for our 2026 RTP Grant
Application.
I have attached our Public Notice, and I am happy to answer any questions.
Our grant application applies to the West crossing bridge replacement of the 5K Loop.

The existing West crossing is an approximately 30-foot wide bridge span, and in fair condition, with
some rotting timbers. Approximately 130-feet downstream of the crossing, there is an approximately
20-foot high cascade that would create a barrier to anadromous fish; this barrier was also noted by
ADF&G in 2020.

These bridges were rated to have a lifespan of 15 to 25 years, and we are replacing the bridges with steel
culverts for the safety of the trails users, groomers, and maintenance vehicles that utilize these
crossings daily. We want to prevent interruption of recreational use of the 5K Nordic Loop, as it serves
as access to the popular Winner Creek Trail.

We have contracted with Anchorage engineering firm HDR, Inc. to survey, design, permit, and manage
this project. HDR Inc utilized their extensive experience with Western Construction to create all cost
estimates for this project. One of the many benefits for using Western Equipment for the construction is
their culvert installation experience in Girdwood, and possible reduction of mobilization costs by being
on site with other local projects.

We are seeking support for the Girdwood Nordic Ski Club’s (GNSC) application for a Recreational Trails
Program grant for improved stream crossings.

Thank you for your consideration,

Deb

                        Of the Girdwood Board of Supervisors

      RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT FOR A RECREATIONAL TRAIL PROGRAM (RTP) GRANT
    APPLICATION FOR GIRDWOOD NORDIC SKI CLUB (GNSC) CULVERT/BRIDGE PROJECTS

   WHEREAS, the Girdwood Nordic Ski Club (GNSC) proposes to replace three log stringer bridges (installed in 2009 and
    2010) with metal culverts over unnamed tributaries of Moose Meadow Creek; and

   WHEREAS, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) has recommended aquatic organism passage for two of
    the crossings to preserve the connection to their upstream habitats, while the third crossing will be designed to
   accommodate trail drainage; and,

   WHEREAS, the GNSC has contracted with HDR, and all streams were assessed by HDR Water Resource Professional
    Engineer (PE) Bill Spencer and Engineer-in-Training (EIT) Kacy Grundhauser on October 18, 2023 and HDR will
    prepare environmental permit applications for the two culvert replacements and pursue a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
   (USACE) Nationwide permit for maintenance activities; and

   WHEREAS, once Alaska Department of Fish and Game Fish Habitat permits and Alaska Department of Natural
    Resources Temporary Water Use Permits are in place, GNSC will hire a contractor and begin replacing the bridges; and,

   WHEREAS, GNSC has a successful record in permitting and completion of capital projects; and

   WHEREAS, this Resolution of Support comes at the recommendation by unanimous consent of the Girdwood Trails
   Committee at their October 1 2024 regular meeting.

   THEREFORE, the Girdwood Board of Supervisors resolves support for Girdwood Nordic Ski Club’s application for
    Recreational Trails Program Grant Funding to replace bridges on the Girdwood Nordic 5K Loop.

   PASSED AND APPROVED by a vote of 4 to 0 this 21st day of October 2024.





    Brian Burnett                                            Attest
   GBOS Parks and Recreation Chair
